The invading forces of Abdali then drove out the Marathas led by Sadashivrao Bhau, deposed Shah Jahan III, the puppet Mughal emperor of Imad-ul-Mulk, and installed Shah Alam II as the rightful emperor.

On 26 December 1530, Humayun succeeded his father Babur to the throne of Delhi as ruler of the Mughal territories in the Indian subcontinent.

items.name: Duleep Singh

items.note: Maharaja Sir Duleep Singh , also spelled Dalip Singh, and later in life nicknamed the "Black Prince of Perthshire", was the last Maharaja of the Sikh Empire. He was Maharaja Ranjit Singh's youngest son, the only child of Maharani Jind Kaur. He was placed in power in September 1843, at the age of five, with his mother ruling on his behalf, and after their defeat in the Anglo-Sikh War, under a British Resident.

items.name: Sher Singh

items.name: Great Wall of China
items.desc: ancient defensive wall across northern China
items.note: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the northern borders of China to protect against invasions. Construction began as early as the 7th century BC, with the most famous sections built by the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644). The wall stretches over 21,000 km, making it the longest man-made structure in the world. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The wall features watchtowers, garrison stations, and beacon towers. Contrary to popular belief, the wall is not visible from space with the naked eye. It attracts over 10 million visitors annually, with the most popular section near Beijing at Badaling.

items.desc: Hyder Ali — medieval India, 1722–1782.
items.note: Hyder Ali was the Sultan and de facto ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore in southern India. He distinguished himself as a soldier, eventually drawing the attention of Mysore's rulers. Rising to the post of Dalavayi to Krishnaraja Wodeyar II, he came to dominate the titular monarch and the Mysore government.

items.name: Shah Alam II
items.desc: Shah Alam II — medieval India, 1728–1806.
items.note: Shah Alam II , also known by his birth name Ali Gohar, or Ali Gauhar, was the seventeenth Mughal emperor and the son of Alamgir II. The reign of Shah Alam saw a number of invasions, the first and foremost by Ahmed Shah Abdali in 1761, which led to the third battle of Panipat between the Maratha Empire and the Afghans under Abdali. The invading forces of Abdali then drove out the Marathas led by Sadashivrao Bhau, deposed Shah Jahan III, the puppet Mughal emperor of Imad-ul-Mulk, and installed Shah Alam II as the rightful emperor.

items.name: Bahadur Shah Zafar
items.desc: Bahadur Shah Zafar — medieval India, 1775–1862.
items.note: Bahadur Shah II , also known by his poetic title Bahadur Shah Zafar , was the twentieth and last Mughal emperor and an Urdu poet. He was a titular emperor with his authority limited to the Walled City of Delhi, but was declared the Emperor of India by the forces opposing East India Company forces in parts of the Indian subcontinent during the Indian Rebellion of 1857. Zafar was exiled to Yangon in British-controlled Burma in December 1857 by the East India Company after rebel defeat in the war, putting an end to the nearly 500-year long Timurid dynasty started by Timur.

items.name: Aurangzeb
items.desc: Aurangzeb — medieval India, 1618–1707.
items.note: Alamgir I , commonly known by the title Aurangzeb, was the sixth Mughal emperor, reigning from 1658 until his death in 1707. Under his reign, the Mughal Empire reached its greatest extent, with territory spanning nearly the entirety of the Indian subcontinent. Aurangzeb and the Mughals belonged to a branch of the Timurid dynasty.

items.desc: Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal
items.note: Shah Jahan I , also called Shah Jahan the Magnificent, was the fifth Mughal Emperor from 1628 until his deposition in 1658. His reign marked the zenith of Mughal architectural and cultural achievements. The third son of Jahangir , Shah Jahan participated in the military campaigns against the Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar and the rebel Lodi nobles of the Deccan.

items.name: Humayun
items.desc: Humayun — medieval India, 1508–1556.
items.note: Nasir al-Din Muhammad , commonly known by his regnal name Humayun , was the second Mughal emperor, who ruled much of what is now eastern Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Northern India, and Pakistan from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to his death in 1556. At the time of his death, the Mughal Empire spanned almost one million square kilometers. On 26 December 1530, Humayun succeeded his father Babur to the throne of Delhi as ruler of the Mughal territories in the Indian subcontinent.

items.name: Jahangir
items.desc: Jahangir — medieval India, 1569–1627.

Aurangzeb and the Mughals belonged to a branch of the Timurid dynasty.

items.name: Shah Alam II
items.desc: Shah Alam II — medieval India, 1728–1806.
items.note: Shah Alam II , also known by his birth name Ali Gohar, or Ali Gauhar, was the seventeenth Mughal emperor and the son of Alamgir II. The reign of Shah Alam saw a number of invasions, the first and foremost by Ahmed Shah Abdali in 1761, which led to the third battle of Panipat between the Maratha Empire and the Afghans under Abdali. The invading forces of Abdali then drove out the Marathas led by Sadashivrao Bhau, deposed Shah Jahan III, the puppet Mughal emperor of Imad-ul-Mulk, and installed Shah Alam II as the rightful emperor.
